title: HACCP & Food Safety Management
blurb: How HACCP keeps food safe: hazards, critical control points, monitoring, corrective action and records, and your part.
siteNotes: The venue's own HACCP plan or Safer Food, Better Business pack and where it is kept

cards.title: HACCP & Food Safety Management
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- say what HACCP is and why we have it
- name the three hazard types and give examples of critical control points
- do your part: follow, record honestly and report

cards.title: HACCP in plain words
cards.body:
HACCP stands for Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points. It is the internationally recognised system we use to keep food safe, and by law every food business must have a food safety management system based on HACCP principles.

The idea is simple: work out where things could go wrong, and put checks in place to stop them.

cards.title: Three kinds of hazard
cards.body: A hazard is anything that could make food unsafe.

items.title: Chemical
items.text: Such as cleaning products getting into food

items.title: Physical
items.text: Such as glass, metal or plastic

cards.title: Critical control points
cards.body: Critical control points (CCPs) are the steps where a check is essential to keep food safe. Each has a critical limit.

items.title: Cooking
items.text: Critical limit, for example a core temperature of 75°C

cards.title: Check, correct, record
cards.body: We monitor the control points by checking and recording temperatures and times. If something falls outside the safe limits, we take corrective action.

items.title: Monitor
items.text: Check and record temperatures and times

items.title: Corrective action
items.text: Cook longer, adjust a fridge, or throw the food away

items.title: Keep records
items.text: Logs and diaries are our proof

cards.title: Everyone does their bit
cards.body:
HACCP is not just paperwork for the chef. It only works if everyone follows the procedures, carries out and honestly records their checks, and reports anything that is not right.

> Report a fridge running warm, or a delivery that arrives too warm.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- HACCP is the system that keeps food safe, and the law requires it
- Hazards are biological, chemical or physical
- CCPs, such as cooking, chilling and hot-holding, need a check and a critical limit
- Outside the limits means corrective action, and records are our proof
- HACCP is everyone's job: follow, record honestly, report

cards.why: HACCP stands for Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points.

cards.q: By law, food businesses must have a food safety system based on HACCP principles.
cards.why: Every food business must have a food safety management system based on HACCP principles.

options: A senior chef who signs off the menu
A cleaning product that is safe near food
A step where a check is essential to keep food safe
A point where deliveries are signed for
cards.why: CCPs are the steps where a check is essential to keep food safe, such as cooking, chilling and hot-holding.

cards.q: Which of these is one of the three types of food hazard?
cards.why: The three groups are biological, chemical and physical.

cards.q: A "critical limit" for cooking might be:
options: Whatever the oven is set to
cards.why: Each CCP has a critical limit, for example cooking to a core temperature of 75°C.

cards.q: If a check falls outside safe limits, you should take corrective action.
cards.why: Corrective action, such as cooking longer, adjusting a fridge or throwing the food away, is how we respond.

cards.q: Why do we keep temperature logs and cleaning diaries?
options: To show the records are filled in each week
To prove that food is being kept safe
To check how long staff spend cleaning
To replace the need for checking temperatures
cards.why: Those records are our proof that food is being kept safe.

cards.q: HACCP is only the chef's responsibility, not everyone's.
cards.why: HACCP only works if everyone follows the procedures, records honestly and reports problems.

cards.q: Which of these is a critical control point in a kitchen?
cards.why: Cooking, chilling and hot-holding are steps where a check is essential.

cards.q: Which of these should you report as part of food safety?
options: A guest asking for the menu
cards.why: Report anything that is not right, like a fridge running warm or a delivery that arrives too warm.
